title: The Disguised Warrior
tagline: She takes her father's armor and rewrites what courage looks like.

scenes.text: Northern Wei Dynasty, 5th century CE. The imperial summons arrives: one man from every family must serve the Khan's army. Hua Mulan's father is old and ill. Her brother too young. So she makes a choice that will pass into legend.

scenes.speaker: Hua Mulan
scenes.text: I will take my father's armor. I will ride his horse. For twelve years the army will know me as a man — and I will fight as well as any of them. Better.

challenge.fact: The Ballad of Mulan, a poem dating to the Northern Wei dynasty (386–534 CE), tells of a daughter who disguises herself as a man to spare her aged, ailing father from conscription. She fights for twelve years, earns high honours, and then reveals her identity — astonishing her comrades.

challenge.instruction: Why does Hua Mulan disguise herself as a man in the Ballad of Mulan? Gather what the story needs: match the goods until the tally is met.

scenes.text: The Ballad of Mulan was first recorded in the 6th century — its origins possibly even older. Whether historical or mythological, Mulan represents the idea that courage and skill belong to neither gender alone.

challenge.fact: The ballad's ending is deliberately understated: Mulan's comrades, who fought beside her for a decade, are stunned to discover she is a woman. The poem asks no moral question — it simply presents her choice as natural and her courage as obvious.

scenes.speaker: Hua Mulan
scenes.text: After twelve years of war, the Emperor offers me a title, a post, wealth. I ask only for a swift horse. I am going home. My family needs me more than the court does.

challenge.fact: Mulan refused the emperor's offer of office and asked only for a fast horse to carry her home. The original ballad ends with her reunited family and Mulan in her women's clothes again — her identity secure, her duty complete, her reward the return of ordinary life.

challenge.instruction: Lead Mulan's cavalry through the northern frontier — avoid ambushes and reach the enemy encampment before dawn.
challenge.fact: The ballad describes a real frontier: the northern Wei territories were under constant pressure from the Rouran Khaganate. The poem's military details — twelve years of campaigns, the yellow river crossing, the Black Mountain pass — reflect genuine geography and the brutal reality of steppe warfare.

challenge.instruction: As a disguised officer earning trust through merit alone, find the decisive move that breaks the enemy's northern line.
challenge.fact: The Ballad of Mulan became one of China's most enduring stories because it celebrated filial piety and personal courage simultaneously — two of Confucian culture's highest values. It has been retold in opera, film, and literature across fourteen centuries.
